blocks.text: Let me start with the one line that made me stop scrolling:
> "An allocation of any future @Arcus token will be reserved for the @dYdX  community."
> — Antonio Juliano(@AntonioMJuliano ), founder of dYdX

Founders don't say things like that casually. That sentence signals two things: an Arcus token is coming, and early participants matter. And right now, Arcus has no token, no TGE date, no points program saturated with mercenary farmers. Just a waitlist, a live spot product, and a founding story that most people haven't connected yet.
➡️ Join the Arcus perps waitlist:
https://waitlist.arcus.xyz/s/NOORUCN

I don't cover perp DEXes unless I genuinely see something. My primary lens is TreadFi — the algorithmic trading terminal I use and cover, which connects CEXes and perp DEXes so retail and institutional traders can run algo execution, market making bots, AI agentic trading, and funding rate arb from one place. Every time a new DEX has integrated with TreadFi — @OndoPerps, @perpltrade  — early TreadFi users got meaningfully rewarded through incentive programs in the first weeks.
Arcus is the next DEX getting integrated into TreadFi. The integration isn't live yet. Which means, if the pattern holds, the window is now.
But before you care about the window, you need to understand what Arcus actually is. And that story starts with a failure.
Part 1: dYdX Won the Battle and Lost the War

Antonio Juliano is a Princeton CS grad and was one of @coinbase 's earliest engineers. He founded dYdX in 2017, and for years it was the decentralized perps exchange. @a16z , @polychain , @paradigm , and @DeFianceCapital  backed it. At its peak, it processed billions in daily volume.
Then @HyperliquidX  showed up with a better product, and every idealistic choice dYdX had made in the name of decentralization turned into a liability:

MEV surface. In dYdX v4, validators run the off-chain orderbook — meaning they see orders before settlement. dYdX openly acknowledged this front-running surface as an unsolved problem. A centralized sequencer simply doesn't have it.
Latency. Orders routing through validator gossip meant 200–400ms round trips. Hyperliquid was sub-100ms. Market makers don't have loyalty. They go where the fills are fastest.
Governance drag. Every new market, fee change, or risk parameter on dYdX required weeks of on-chain governance. Hyperliquid shipped new perp markets in days.
Token headwinds. VC unlocks created persistent sell pressure. Trading incentives attracted wash traders instead of real volume. Retail never built conviction.
The scoreboard today: DYDX trades around $0.12, down more than 99% from its all-time high. HYPE sits at a $13B+ market cap.
Here's the part I respect. Antonio didn't spin it. From the Arcus launch post:
> "dYdX Chain achieved real decentralization… But it also made clear the tradeoffs. Performance and user experience suffered. The market clearly responded."
That's rare founder honesty. And the strategically correct response wasn't to fight Hyperliquid head-on for crypto perps from a weaker liquidity position.
It was to go where Hyperliquid isn't.
Part 2: The Consumer Product Guy
That's where Eddie Zhang(@epic_edge_ ) comes in.
Eddie's background isn't DeFi-native, and that's exactly the point:
@Meta  — built on Facebook Messenger (1B+ users)
@amazon
Co-founded Fam (social app)
Co-founded Pocket Protector — a Telegram-based social trading bot that hit $1B+ annualized volume with 50,000 users in its first year, backed by Electric Capital and Dragonfly
dYdX Labs acquired Pocket Protector. When Arcus spun out, Eddie became its CEO and founder.
Two quotes tell you how he thinks:
> "The average person downloads 1 app a month and spends 9 seconds using it. Watch someone try your app for 9 seconds and see how far you get."
> "Robinhood feels like Vlad: allergic to friction, obsessed with making a hard thing feel effortless for someone who's never done it. I think about what ours says about us constantly."
He's explicitly modeling Arcus on Robinhood's consumer DNA — backed by nearly a decade of dYdX's DeFi infrastructure knowledge underneath.

And Antonio, on why he handed over the keys: "He's earned my trust as a founder and the team's trust as a leader. The best move for me, for the team, and for the dYdX community is Arcus — with Eddie at the helm."

Most DeFi products are built by engineers for engineers. Arcus is being built by someone who shipped products for a billion people, for users who have never seen an orderbook. When your distribution partner has 25 million retail users, that difference is the entire game.
Part 3: What Arcus Actually Is
One self-custodied account. Two products:
1. Stock Tokens — spot, zero fees, 24/7
95 tokenized equities: TSLA, NVDA, AAPL, SPY, and more. Backed 1:1 by real shares held in custody by Alpaca Securities. No commissions. Ever.
2. Cross-margined perps — up to 50x, 24/7
Equities, crypto, commodities, indices — all margined from a single account. 35 markets and growing.
The workflow this unlocks: hold NVDA spot, run a leveraged TSLA position against it, hedge with an index perp — all from one wallet, all on-chain.
Two Markets, Two Engines
The design detail I like most is that Arcus didn't force one execution model onto everything:
Perps → CLOB. Perps trade 24/7 with continuous flow, and price discovery happens on the book itself. Market makers can rest orders with confidence. A central limit order book is the right tool.

Stock Tokens → RFQ. Here's the subtle problem: stock tokens track equities that close at 4pm ET. A resting order placed Friday afternoon can be badly stale by Sunday night — so makers either quote defensively wide or don't rest orders at all. RFQ flips it: you request a quote, professional market makers compete in real time for your exact size, and you only sign after seeing the price. No AMM slippage. Best execution at any size.
As Eddie puts it: "Makers compete for your trade instead of you fighting for a fill."
The Architecture Choice
Under the hood, Arcus made a deliberate call that separates it from both Hyperliquid and dYdX v4: off-chain matching, on-chain settlement.

The honest physics: a fully on-chain orderbook means every order passes through blockchain consensus — 200ms+ block times minimum, no matter how few validators you run. Even Hyperliquid, with roughly 16 validators and tight hardware requirements, can't hit CEX-grade latency. Tightening block times requires more hardware centralization, which defeats the point.
Arcus's stack instead:
Off-chain matching engine: 20ms confirmations, 100,000+ orders/second — genuine CEX-grade speed
Appchain validators independently re-verify every block: state transitions, order signatures, oracle prices
Custody and settlement on Robinhood Chain — an EVM L2 inheriting Ethereum security

Your funds sit in smart contracts that only move if the math checks out. The operator cannot steal them — but execution speed doesn't wait for consensus. It's essentially the model that made dYdX v3 on StarkEx work, revisited with validator verification and a purpose-built L2 instead of Ethereum mainnet.
Not a compromise. The right framework to scale.
Part 4: The Robinhood Angle — Honestly Framed
Robinhood Crypto made a strategic equity investment in Arcus. Amount undisclosed — but it's a shareholder relationship. Robinhood has direct financial upside in Arcus growing.

Now, full transparency, because I'd rather you hear it from me: Robinhood also invested in Lighter (via Robinhood Ventures, in Lighter's $68M Series B). The Robinhood Chain DEX ecosystem is multi-player — Uniswap, 1inch, Arcus, Rialto, and Lighter all operate on it. Arcus's edge isn't exclusivity. It's depth of alignment.
Arcus vs. @Lighter_xyz  — The Honest Comparison

Lighter is genuinely impressive: ZK rollup, 45M operations/day, a top-3 perp DEX globally. Its Robinhood partnership (50/50 revenue share, $11M in LIT incentives) grew out of a 12-year personal relationship between Lighter's Vlad Novakovski and Robinhood's Vlad Tenev. That relationship is real and deep. I'm not dismissing it.
But if you're asking where the upside from today sits:

Lighter already did its major distribution. TGE was December 30, 2025. 25% of supply went to Season 1 and 2 point farmers. The $11M Robinhood-user incentive is their next push. Most of the early-mover window for LIT has closed.
Arcus has no token yet. None. And the team has publicly committed an allocation to the dYdX community — which, by extension, signals that early users, traders, and waitlist participants matter.

Arcus is natively built around Robinhood. Lighter is excellent perp infrastructure that plugged into Robinhood Chain. Arcus was incubated specifically for that ecosystem — stock tokens, equity perps, RFQ execution designed for retail fills. Those aren't the same thing.

My read: Lighter got its early-mover moment and rewarded the people who showed up. I'm giving that same attention to Arcus at the same stage. I could be wrong. But the incentive window is clearly wider here.
The Ondo Parallel — Framed Correctly

I've covered @OndoPerps  Perps extensively, so let me be precise rather than lazy: Ondo is actually more vertically integrated than Arcus in tokenized equities, not less. Ondo issues its own tokenized securities directly — TSLAon, NVDAon, SPYon — through Ondo Global Markets (BVI) Limited, across Ethereum, Solana, and BNB Chain, with its own perps platform where those stocks work as collateral.
So Ondo = issuer + venue + perps. Arcus = the trading venue built on Robinhood-issued stock tokens. Not the issuer — the best place to trade.
The thesis rhymes, but the moats differ. Arcus's moat isn't who issued the stock. It's who has 25 million retail users behind them and a consumer-grade product to onboard them.
Distribution beats vertical integration when Robinhood's brand is the distribution.
Part 5: The @tread_fi  Angle — Why My Audience Is Here

TreadFi (tread.fi) is a high-performance algorithmic trading terminal and OEMS. It currently connects CEXes — Binance, Bybit, OKX, Bitget, Deribit, Gate — alongside perp DEXes including Hyperliquid, Perpl, Ondo, and Paradex.
When a DEX integrates with TreadFi, it gets an instant injection of sophisticated flow:
Institutional-grade algo traders running TWAP/VWAP on the orderbook
Market making bots deepening the CLOB
Funding rate arbitrageurs anchoring perp prices to spot
AI agents and multi-venue strategy runners

And what TreadFi users historically get in return: incentives. Both Ondo and Perpl ran meaningful reward programs for TreadFi traders in their early integration periods. Volume + liquidity flowed in; the people who showed up first got paid.

Arcus is next in that pipeline. The integration isn't live yet — which means the setup for TreadFi users is: before the liquidity flows, before the incentives kick in, before the wider community piles in.
Part 6: Go Look at It Yourself
Don't take my word on the product. Open the app.

The UI is genuinely the best I've seen on a perp DEX — clean, fast, consumer-grade. That's not an accident. It's what happens when someone who built for a billion users, who believes first impressions are decided in nine seconds, ships a trading product.
The Summary — Three Reasons I'm Positioned
1. No token yet. Antonio has publicly committed an allocation to the dYdX community. Early Arcus activity is the most obvious way to be counted when that materializes.
2. TreadFi integration incoming. The Ondo and Perpl pattern is clear: early TreadFi users on newly integrated DEXes get rewarded. The integration isn't live yet. That's the window.
3. The waitlist is already 40,000+ deep for perps access — but spot trading is open today. Establishing presence now beats arriving after perps open to everyone.

The dYdX story ended with a hard lesson: decentralization purity doesn't win markets — product and distribution do. Arcus is that lesson, rebuilt from scratch, with Robinhood's 25 million users on the other side of the door.
